subject: Incident: Token double-counting affecting CloudPilot billing
messages:
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@cloudpilot.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Incident: Token double-counting affecting CloudPilot billing

Alex —

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. I wanted to follow up with a concise summary and next steps while we investigate the billing anomalies you observed.

What happened (short): During a rolling deploy of an internal batching optimization on Aug 17 at ~14:30 PDT, a regression caused some requests to be accounted twice in our token metering layer for a narrow window (~14:30–15:00 PDT). The runtime itself returned correct responses; the user-facing behavior was unaffected. The error is strictly in accounting (token counting) not in model sampling.

Scope: Our preliminary run indicates approximately 0.7% of CloudPilot’s tokens during that half-hour were double-counted, which could surface as inflated usage on your July–August invoices depending on request timing. I have attached a per-request export for the window we believe is affected (usage-export-20260817.csv).

Immediate actions we have taken:
- Reverted the batching change and rolled back the counting fix at 15:05 PDT.
- Disabled the new metering path and added additional checks to prevent double-counting.
- Started a per-customer reconciliation job; we’ll produce an adjustment file for you with linked invoice items.

Proposed remediation for CloudPilot:
1) We will generate a credit equal to the overcounted tokens plus 10% margin to be conservative.
2) We will apply the credit to your next invoice and can also issue an immediate invoice credit note if you prefer.
3) We’ll share a postmortem and the reconciliation CSV with line-item mapping to the invoice.

Can you confirm you are OK with that approach? If you prefer immediate cash refund or a different accounting mechanism (e.g., separate refund invoice), say the word and we’ll route to finance for prioritization.

Attached: usage-export-20260817.csv (per-request token rows for 14:00–15:30 PDT), invoice-202607.pdf (your last invoice for reference).

I’ll keep Laura and Markus in the loop — they’re handling credits and invoice updates. We’ll follow up with exact credit numbers by tomorrow morning.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Soojin —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the export. We’re reviewing the CSV now but two quick asks while you reconcile:

1) Can you provide an estimate of the dollar impact (rough ballpark) so we can inform finance and pause any automated collections if needed?
2) Please do not charge or invoice any disputed items while this is being reconciled — our billing team wants the overage isolated.

We appreciate the proposed 10% margin on top of the overcount — that helps. If it’s easier, we’d prefer a formal credit note applied to the August invoice rather than a refund.

Alex Taylor
Head of Platform, CloudPilot Inc.
alex.taylor@cloudpilot.com | +1 (206) 555-3421

Team —

I reviewed the reconciliation job Soojin kicked off. Short recommendation below so we can reply to CloudPilot with a concrete number:

Summary of numbers (preliminary):
- Total tokens in window (CloudPilot): 4,120,430
- Estimated double-counted tokens: 32,842 (0.8%)
- Unit price (effective on their plan): $0.00025 per token
- Raw overcharge: $8.21
- Proposed credit (including 10% buffer): $9.03 -> round to $9.05 for the credit note

Recommendation: Issue a credit note for $9.05, apply to August invoice, and mark disputed items as "waived" in billing system. Because this is a small absolute amount, I suggest we also proactively offer a one-time service credit of $250 as a customer goodwill for operational impact and time spent by their team reviewing the export. That has executive approval.

Attachments: credit-notes-draft.pdf (draft credit note and AR memo). If Finance approves an immediate refund instead of a credit note, we’ll notify CloudPilot.

@Markus please approve the $250 goodwill credit. @Rishi please route the $9.05 accounting adjustment in the billing ledger and tag it to CP-2025-8342.

Thanks —
Laura
Director, Customer Finance — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@cloudpilot.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Incident: Token double-counting affecting CloudPilot billing

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Quick update and the concrete actions we took: 

What we did:
- Final reconciliation completed (attached). Confirmed 32,842 overcounted tokens for the affected window; unit price matched to your plan.
- Applied a credit note in the amount of $9.05 to your August invoice (invoice 202607).
- Additionally applied a one-time goodwill credit of $250 to your account as a courtesy.

Timeline / Financials:
- Credit note issued and visible in your billing portal immediately; the accounting adjustment will reflect in your next statement cycle. If you need an immediate refund instead, Laura is available to process it (finance will need a signed refund form).

Root cause and remediation:
- Root cause: a regression in the batching-to-metering handoff introduced duplicate token increments when a narrow class of concurrent streams overlapped during a rolling deploy.
- Remediation: fix reverted, additional automated checks added to the metering path, and a lightweight canary for counting behavior deployed. We’ve also added a nightly reconciliation job for high-volume customers to catch discrepancies earlier.

Postmortem and next steps:
- Full postmortem: https://internal.redwoodinference.com/postmortems/token-accounting-20260817 (public summary to follow in 7 days).
- Reconciliation CSV and the credit note are attached.

If you’d like a short call to walk through the reconciliation CSV with our billing team and engineering, I can set that up this week. Sorry for the disruption — we take these very seriously and appreciate you working with us.

Best,
Soojin
